nodes.summary: The bijection on unordered pairs of sites induced by the quarter-turn rotation `(a, b) ↦ (-b, a)`. It maps lattice edges to lattice edges, but not to the dual edge crossing them: `{(0,0), (1,0)}` goes to `{(0,0), (0,1)}`. For the geometric crossing use `sharedPrimalEdge`.
nodes.title: Quarter-turn rotation of unordered site pairs

nodes.summary: The bijection between primal and dual edges induced by `rot90Iso`.
nodes.title: Bijection between primal and dual edges

nodes.summary: The configuration in which `e` is open exactly when the inverse quarter turn `crossEdge.symm e` of `e` is closed in `ω`. This is the dual configuration only up to the rotation: applying it twice gives the half-turn of `ω` (`dualConfig_dualConfig`), not `ω`.
nodes.title: Rotated dual configuration

nodes.summary: The dual square lattice. Its vertices are the face centres of `ℤ²`, relabelled as integer points, so as a graph it is `hypercubicLattice 2`.
nodes.title: Dual square lattice

nodes.summary: The quarter-turn rotation as a permutation of `ℤ²`.
nodes.title: Quarter-turn rotation as a permutation

nodes.summary: The quarter-turn rotation `(a, b) ↦ (-b, a)` of `ℤ²`.
nodes.title: Quarter-turn rotation of the square lattice

nodes.summary: The inverse quarter-turn rotation `(a, b) ↦ (b, -a)` of `ℤ²`.
nodes.title: Inverse quarter-turn rotation

nodes.summary: The quarter-turn rotation as a graph automorphism of the square lattice.
nodes.title: Quarter-turn rotation as a lattice automorphism

nodes.summary: The isomorphism between the square lattice and its dual given by the quarter-turn rotation.
nodes.title: Rotational self-duality of the square lattice

nodes.summary: The identity isomorphism between the square lattice and its dual.
nodes.title: Identity self-duality of the square lattice

nodes.summary: An equivalence `α ≃ β` induces an equivalence of unordered pairs `Sym2 α ≃ Sym2 β`.
nodes.title: Unordered pairs under an equivalence

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
